points.t: A child with fever, sore throat and a fine rough red rash starting on the neck and chest, accentuated in skin folds, with a strawberry tongue.
Phenoxymethylpenicillin for 10 days (clarithromycin if allergic), exclusion from school until 24 h of antibiotics, notify UKHSA, safety-net for invasive GAS.
Invasive group A streptococcal disease, and Kawasaki disease or toxic shock as differentials.

points: Abrupt **fever**, **sore throat** (exudative tonsillitis, tender anterior cervical nodes), headache, nausea/vomiting, abdominal pain.
**Tongue:** day 1–2 **"white strawberry tongue"** (white coat with red papillae poking through) → day 3–5 **"red strawberry/raspberry tongue"** (coat sheds). Palatal petechiae (Forchheimer spots).
Rash fades in ~1 week, followed by **desquamation** of fingertips, toes, groin.

**Causes of strawberry tongue:** scarlet fever; **Kawasaki disease**; **toxic shock syndrome** (staph or strep); also reported with vitamin B12/folate deficiency (glossitis), yellow fever, allergy/drug reactions and some other infections.

cards.name: Kawasaki disease
cards.clue: **Fever ≥5 days**, bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, red cracked lips, strawberry tongue, swollen red hands/feet then peeling, polymorphous rash, cervical node; <5 years — **urgent paediatric referral** (coronary aneurysm risk)

cards.name: Toxic shock syndrome
cards.clue: Hypotension, multi-organ involvement, diffuse "sunburn" erythroderma, tampon/wound source — **999/ED**

cards.name: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
cards.clue: Tender erythema, flaccid blisters, Nikolsky positive, perioral crusting, no tonsillitis

cards.name: Viral exanthems (measles, rubella, enterovirus, parvovirus "slapped cheek")
cards.clue: Measles: coryza, cough, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots; slapped cheek: lacy limb rash; no sandpaper texture

cards.name: Infectious mononucleosis (± amoxicillin rash)
cards.clue: Teenager, marked lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, rash after amoxicillin

cards.name: Miliaria / heat rash
cards.clue: Tiny papules in covered areas, afebrile

points: Paracetamol/ibuprofen for fever and throat pain (avoid ibuprofen if dehydrated or chickenpox co-infection per local advice), fluids, soft foods, emollient for itch/peeling.

NHS **Pharmacy First** (England) acute sore throat pathway uses FeverPAIN for pharyngitis; check the current pathway on how suspected scarlet fever is handled (typically outside PGD scope → prescriber/GP).

rungs.k: First-line antibiotics (to speed recovery, reduce transmission and complications)
points: **Phenoxymethylpenicillin for 10 days** (BNF age-banded doses; e.g. adults/children ≥12 years 500 mg four times daily, or 1 g twice daily per local guidance).

Penicillin allergy: **clarithromycin** (5 days) or **azithromycin** (per BNF/local guidance); **amoxicillin** (10 days) is an alternative where liquid palatability/supply is an issue (follow UKHSA/local advice during shortages).

rungs.k: Red flags / refer — safety-net for invasive GAS
points: Quinsy (trismus, uvula deviation), otitis media, sinusitis, cervical abscess, pneumonia.

Late: **acute rheumatic fever** (2–4 weeks; arthritis, carditis), **post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis** (1–3 weeks; dark urine, oedema, hypertension), **PANDAS** (rare), and the link to **guttate psoriasis**.
Features of Kawasaki (fever ≥5 days, conjunctivitis) or TSS (hypotension) → urgent.

items.t: Rapid deterioration, severe pain, a spreading skin infection, breathing difficulty or signs of sepsis: **invasive GAS**, emergency.
Fever for 5 days or more with red eyes, red lips, swollen hands and feet: consider **Kawasaki disease**.
Chickenpox plus scarlet fever in the same household: higher invasive GAS risk, so lower threshold for review.

pearls.t: "Sandpaper rash + sore throat + strawberry tongue + circumoral pallor" = scarlet fever until proven otherwise; on darker skin rely on texture and the tongue.
Strawberry tongue is **not specific** — a child with ≥5 days of fever and red eyes needs Kawasaki excluded.
Phenoxymethylpenicillin is best taken on an empty stomach; four-times-daily dosing needs adherence support (use bd regimen where appropriate).
Tell parents peeling of fingers/toes 1–2 weeks later is expected.
Safety-net clearly and in writing for iGAS symptoms; advise urine check/return if dark urine or swelling after 1–3 weeks.
